newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus prime minister offers resignation.
newsitem.headline: Belarus prime minister offers resignation.

text.p: Belarussian Prime Minister Mikhail Chigir has threatened to resign if President Alexander Lukashenko goes ahead with a November 24 referendum to increase his powers, the deputy speaker of parliament said on Monday.
Gennady Karpenko, speaking to reporters after meeting Chigir with other parliamentary leaders, quoted the premier as saying he would resign unless Lukashenko agreed to a number of conditions.
"Chigir has set the president economic and political conditions including cancelling the referendum," Karpenko said.
Chigir's departure would be a big blow to Lukashenko. He was appointed prime minister after Lukashenko's landslide election win in July 1994 and is seen as a presidential loyalist.
Chigir, emerging from the meeting with parliamentarians, neither confirmed nor denied he had resigned, saying: "Not so fast, not so fast".
Lukashenko is locked in a power struggle with parliament, the constitutional court and other bodies, who accuse him of trying to impose dictatorship.

Police clashed with opposition demonstrators in Minsk on Sunday. Lukashenko was campaigning in Gomel, southern Belarus, near the Ukrainian border, on Monday and made no immediate comment on his premier's apparent withdrawal of support.
